summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is retained: small short-term osteoarthritis pain benefits in mostly low-quality trials, with the ACR 2026 recommendation against and the VA/DoD 2026 insufficient-evidence finding. Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 rulings and the shared OA supplement standard (OA_SUPPLEMENT_STANDARD.md; ACR Sept 2026 strongly against; VA/DoD May 2026 insufficient evidence for or against), this is a completed no-credit on the reference path, reversing the earlier draft credit. The 2015 Cochrane review (43 RCTs, 9,110 participants, oral chondroitin in mostly knee osteoarthritis) found a small short-term pain benefit versus placebo at >=800 mg/day (MD -10.1/100, low quality) plus positive Lequesne, WOMAC MCII and joint-space outcomes, with uncertain long-term pain benefit and loss of significance in some sensitivity analyses. The context keeps these true directions (short-term pain positive, long-term pain mixed) with scoring_eligible false; the record becomes reference-only, which removes Evidence points from chondroitin products.

record_updates.effect_direction_rationale: Shared OA supplement standard (2026-10-28): the ACR 2026 guideline strongly recommends against glucosamine, chondroitin and their combination for knee, hip and hand OA (certainty low for glucosamine alone, moderate for the combination), and the VA/DoD 2026 guideline (Recommendation 30) finds insufficient evidence for or against them (very low confidence; effects likely below a clinically meaningful difference). Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling, glucosamine and chondroitin records use one standard: completed no-credit on the reference path with true source directions retained; exact-preparation findings are recorded but do not create retail-supplement credit.

identity.chemical_form: chondroitin sulfate; monotherapy and combinations kept separate in source analyses

population.description: Adults with osteoarthritis, mostly knee, with few hip and hand trials; 43 randomized trials, 4,962 chondroitin and 4,148 control participants; trial duration 1 month to 3 years (Abstract; Results).

study_contexts.study_design: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized or quasi-randomized trials of oral chondroitin versus placebo or active comparator; this context uses the chondroitin-versus-placebo summary-of-findings analyses restricted to doses of at least 800 mg/day.

outcomes.name: Pain 0-100, short-term (<6 months), chondroitin >=800 mg/d vs placebo: MD -10.14 (95% CI -14.58 to -5.71), 8 studies, 1077 participants; low-quality evidence, I2 70%
Pain 0-100, long-term (>=6 months): MD -9.01 (95% CI -17.68 to -0.34), 6 studies, 989 participants; low quality; authors uncertain whether pain is reduced
WOMAC MCII pain response (>=20% reduction), long-term: RR 1.12 (1.01-1.24), 2 studies, 1253 participants; high quality
Lequesne index, short-term: SMD -0.57 (-0.84 to -0.30), 7 studies, 903 participants; moderate quality
Minimum joint space width loss, long-term: 4.7% less relative to placebo (1.6%-7.8%), 2 studies

limitations: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is retained: small short-term osteoarthritis pain benefits in mostly low-quality trials, with the ACR 2026 recommendation against and the VA/DoD 2026 insufficient-evidence finding.

Shared OA supplement standard (2026-10-28): the ACR 2026 guideline strongly recommends against glucosamine, chondroitin and their combination for knee, hip and hand OA (certainty low for glucosamine alone, moderate for the combination), and the VA/DoD 2026 guideline (Recommendation 30) finds insufficient evidence for or against them (very low confidence; effects likely below a clinically meaningful difference). Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling, glucosamine and chondroitin records use one standard: completed no-credit on the reference path with true source directions retained; exact-preparation findings are recorded but do not create retail-supplement credit.

Exact-preparation evidence: the Cochrane benefit was uncertain when restricted to studies without pharmaceutical funding, with adequate allocation concealment or with >200 participants (Abstract); trial chondroitin preparations (e.g. pharmaceutical products such as Structum and Chondrosulf) cannot be equated with retail supplements.

Benefit was uncertain when analyses were limited to adequate allocation concealment, large samples (>200) or no pharmaceutical funding (Abstract Main results); mostly low-quality, highly heterogeneous short-term trials.
Pooled heterogeneous study regimens; >=800 mg/day is the summary-of-findings analysis stratum, not a validated efficacy minimum or optimum.
Combination (chondroitin plus glucosamine or other supplement) analyses are kept separate and not credited to chondroitin alone; combination function was null.
Osteoarthritis symptom evidence only; no transfer to general joint health, longevity or prevention in people without osteoarthritis.
Earlier returned decision: date-restricted hold (publication-age-only exclusions withdrawn); superseded for credit by the 2026-10-28 ruling.
Topical multi-ingredient cream; source Results explicitly excludes cream from oral analyses. Identity verified; not an oral chondroitin intervention.

dose.administration_frequency: Study-specific daily oral regimens (e.g. 400 mg three times daily, 500 mg twice daily); no single pooled frequency.
dosage_forms: oral capsule, tablet or sachet (trial-specific preparations)
co_therapies: Trial-specific rescue analgesics/NSAIDs permitted in some trials; no assigned co-therapy in placebo comparisons.
dose.reported_regimen: Results: most studies gave oral chondroitin 800 mg/day or higher, with exceptions below 800 mg/day; summary-of-findings chondroitin-vs-placebo analyses restricted to >=800 mg/day; example arms Structum 500 mg twice daily and Chondrosulf 400 mg three times daily; one topical cream trial excluded from analyses.

normalization.basis: No scalar pooled dose; >=800 mg/day is the review's analysis stratum, not a universal threshold.
